title: Thermodynamic Bounds on Infrared-Modulated ATP Synthesis: Separating Photothermal Heating, Passive Polaritonic Catalysis, and Coherent Ratchets at 71 THz
abstract: Continuing ARR-2025-2AQXS44H6Z8GQAG2 and ARR-2026-1E91AXEJYT890TQC, we establish sharp, machine-checked thermodynamic bounds separating four physical mechanisms for the ~10% cellular ATP enhancement reported under weak 71/87-THz mid-IR irradiation (unrefereed preprint bioRxiv:10.64898/2026.09.10.750628v1): stoichiometric photon-to-ATP conversion, polaritonic catalysis (separating dark-cavity vacuum ZPE from irradiance-driven resonant catalysis), micro-hotspot vs bulk photothermal heating, and active coherent ratchets. Backed by MITO-ATP-MODULATION-CERT-1.0 (20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems with -DwarningAsError=true, 0 sorry, 0 grind, 0 Classical.choice; AST-audited zero-float verifier; 16 SHA-256 certificates C01-C16; and 58 adversarial pytest checks), we prove: (i) First-Law stoichiometric floor > 1.765 absorbed 71-THz photons/ATP (tightened by Carnot efficiency); (ii) exact Mercator brackets pinning |Delta E_a|_10% in (2.545, 2.547) meV at 310 K, compared to the explicitly derived resonant Hopfield A^2 ZPE shift Delta E_ZPE = (128/71) h*THz approx 7.456 meV (> 2.92x as a collective ceiling, subject to 1/N dilution and requiring driven IR excitation over dark controls), forcing +10% ATP-coupled OCR (>= +7.5% total cellular OCR up to 25% proton leak); (iii) exact finite-difference Arrhenius Delta T_10% in (1.52, 1.54) K and pi-free micro-hotspot flux floor I_micro = 4*kappa_th*Delta T/R > 734 W/cm^2 (> 73,400x above 10 mW/cm^2 mid-IR) vs >= 2000x bulk dish amplification; (iv) Barato-Seifert TUR and exact additive ratchet power conservation P_maint + P_ATP <= P_in; and (v) a four-protocol experimental discriminator matrix.
